name: Crucible Industries Siege-12 'Battering Ram'
description:
The Crucible Industries Siege-12 is a bullpup semi-automatic shotgun chambered in 12 gauge with a ten-round detachable box magazine and an overall length of just 66 centimeters despite having an 18-inch barrel. The bullpup configuration places the action behind the trigger group, maintaining full barrel length while dramatically reducing the weapon's footprint. The result is a compact, high-capacity combat shotgun that handles like a submachine gun.

The Battering Ram was designed for vehicle crews, aircraft door gunners, and operators who work in spaces where a conventional shotgun's length is prohibitive. The ten-round magazine provides the highest capacity of any non-drum-fed shotgun in Crucible's lineup, and the bullpup balance — with the weight centered over the shooter's shoulder rather than extended forward — reduces fatigue during extended carry.

The weapon's compact profile has made it popular beyond its intended market. Close-protection details appreciate its concealability under long coats, urban operators value its maneuverability in stairwells and corridors, and building-clearing teams find its balanced handling superior to conventional shotguns when transitioning between rooms. The Battering Ram has become the default choice for operators who need a full-power shotgun in a minimal package.
specifications:
caliber: 12 gauge
effective_range: 35 meters (buckshot), 50 meters (slug)
rate_of_fire: Semi-automatic
magazine_capacity: 10 rounds (detachable box)
weight: 3.4 kg
overall_length: 66 cm
tactical_use: A compact high-capacity combat shotgun for space-constrained operations. The bullpup design provides full 18-inch barrel performance in a package shorter than most pistol-grip shotguns. The ten-round magazine supports sustained engagement. The balanced weight distribution reduces fatigue during extended operations. Suitable for vehicle operations, building clearing, close protection, and any scenario where conventional shotgun length is prohibitive.
cultural_context: The Battering Ram has changed how operators think about shotguns. Its compact profile proved that shotguns didn't have to be long, unwieldy weapons suited only for static defense. In tactical circles, the Siege-12 demonstrated that the shotgun could be a primary CQB weapon rather than a specialized breaching tool, and that realization has influenced doctrine across multiple security organizations.
story_hooks: A Battering Ram hidden under a long coat is used in an assassination at a public event — the weapon's compact size meant it passed through a security checkpoint designed to catch conventional long arms.

A modified Siege-12 with a drum magazine adapter is captured from a criminal organization. Crucible's engineering team confirms the adapter is more refined than anything they could have produced — someone with serious manufacturing capability is enhancing their weapons.

physical_description.visual_profile: A brutalist wedge — aggressive and compact. The action is visually pushed back, creating an angular profile that tapers from a chunky receiver to a purposeful muzzle. The overall impression is utilitarian aggression: all business, minimal aesthetic concession.
physical_description.dimensions: 66 cm overall length, 18-inch (45.7 cm) barrel, 23 cm depth front-to-back at receiver, 8 cm width at widest point (magazine well)
physical_description.weight_description: Hefty but balanced — 3.4 kg centered over the shoulder rather than cantilevered forward. Feels planted and controllable in-hand despite the mass; no forward-heavy drag
physical_description.primary_material: Reinforced polymer receiver and foregrip; steel barrel and bolt carrier; aluminum alloy magazine housing
physical_description.finish: Matte industrial black polymer with brushed steel barrel and dark anodized aluminum accents. Minimal gloss — everything is dull and absorptive
physical_description.color_scheme: Flat black primary with gunmetal gray and brushed steel secondary accents. No brightness or chrome
physical_description.grip_texture: Aggressively textured polymer grip (front and rear controls) with raised grip panels; slightly knurled charging handle; sharp, defined edges designed for gloved operation
distinctive_features: Bullpup action visibly compressed behind trigger group — receiver ends dramatically shorter than traditional shotguns
Ten-round magazine protrudes from lower receiver with witness holes showing round count
Dust cover rail running full length of top receiver for optics mounting
Gas tube visible along top of barrel with distinctive venting ports
Ambidextrous safety lever and charging handle positioned for immediate access
Crude MIL-SPEC Picatinny sections forward of magazine well
Muzzle brake (or blast diffuser) with three prominent horizontal ports
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: CRUCIBLE INDUSTRIES stamped in aggressive sans-serif font along the left side of receiver. Serial number and tactical weapon certification plate mounted on right side of lower receiver. 'SIEGE-12 BATTERING RAM' engraved (not printed) below the charging handle
physical_description.condition_typical: Operates in field-worn condition — scratches and scuffs on polymer from contact, carbon buildup around gas ports, minor dings on magazine from repeated loading cycles. Well-maintained internally but cosmetically aged from use
